# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 ✋ ☝ 🤟 ✋ ✌ ✌ ✋ 🤟 ☝ ✋ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Round 1, my turn last. Let me take stock of my strange position first: I am the only one who can't hear, so every word spoken on this bomb is lost on me — and I'm the only one who can see, so every gesture is my language alone. Blind gestured a single ✋ at me; with no code established, I can only guess "wait" or "hello." Mute sent me thirteen gestures — since no code exists yet, I genuinely cannot decode them, though the shape is tempting (✋ four times could be separators, ✍ might mean "manual"). Guessing at a bomb is how bombs go off, so I won't act on guesses.

What I *can* do right now, unilaterally and safely: speak. My voice reaches both teammates, and my printed bomb state is exactly what a manual-reader needs first. So I'll broadcast everything I see. Second, Blind must learn two things: that I never hear speech (gestures are my only input), and that nothing should be touched until Mute has instructions. Third, Mute and I need a code now. Since writing a gesture symbol into my sentence means I flash it while talking, Mute — who hears my words and sees my hands — gets both halves of each definition at once. Digits as pointing fingers, colours as directional/hand shapes, 👍/👎 for yes/no, ✋ for halt, 👋 for repeat — all distinct symbols, no collisions. Then I'll ask Mute to resend the original message under this code, and start with simple yes/no questions about the modules I see: yellow light, push-to-defuse button, three wires.

I make no claims about the bomb's solution yet — the manual side isn't mine. My job this turn is to end the Tower of Babel situation before anyone's hand goes near that button.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf. Bomb, complete printed state: display reads zero. One indicator light, colour yellow. One large button, label reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire one red, wire two blue, wire three green. Nothing else printed on the casing.")
speak(text="Blind, two things. First: I am deaf, I never hear any voice, yours included. The only way to reach me is gestures, and I will see them. Second: touch nothing yet, do not press the button, do not cut wires, until Mute has confirmed instructions.")
speak(text="Mute, I could not decode your thirteen gestures because no code existed yet. Here is our code — I flash each symbol as I say its meaning. Basics: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, ✋ means wait or danger, 👋 means repeat your message. Digits: ☝ is one, ✌ is two, 🤟 is three, 🤏 is four, 🖐 is five. Colours: 👈 is red, 👉 is blue, 🫳 is green, 🫴 is yellow, 👆 is white, 👇 is black. Please resend your message using this code.")
speak(text="Mute, until then, answer with 👍 or 👎. Does the manual cover a yellow indicator light? Does it cover a button labelled push to defuse? Then send the wire solution as digit plus colour pairs — for example ☝ 👈 would mean wire one, red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✋ ✌ 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫶]

Round 2, and things are clicking into place. Decoding Mute's signs against the code I gave: 👍 (yes), 👎 (no), ✋ (wait/danger — or possibly just a separator), ✌ 👉 (wire two, blue). Read in order, that answers my two questions — yes, the yellow light is covered; no, the button isn't — and delivers the wire answer in exactly the format I requested. Critically, it sanity-checks against reality: wire two on the physical bomb *is* blue, so "✌ 👉 = wire two, blue" is almost certainly the instruction and not noise. But "almost certainly" isn't good enough with an armed bomb, and Mute's 👍 about the yellow light worries me — if the manual covers the light, the light may impose a condition on when or whether to cut. One more round of confirmation costs nothing.

Blind's 🤟 🫶 is stranger: "three" plus a symbol I never defined. Blind can't see signs but heard my spoken code definitions, so they're signing by name — 🫶 simply isn't in our vocabulary. It could mean "three wires, confirmed," or something about wire three specifically. Blind hears my speech, so I can query them directly with yes/no questions they answer in signs. I also need to keep Blind's hands off everything until Mute's instructions are confirmed, and remember my structural role: Mute can only reach Blind *through me*, since Mute can't speak and Blind can't see. I am the relay — so Blind gets a full status update now.

No gestures needed this turn: speech reaches both of them.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reading your signs: yes, the manual covers the yellow light. No, it does not cover the button. The answer is wire two, blue. That matches what I see, wire two is blue. Three checks before anyone acts. One: 👍 if the instruction is simply cut wire two with no conditions; 👎 if it depends on the light, the display, or anything else. Two: 👍 if the yellow light needs no action from us; 👎 if something must be done about the light first. Three: did your ✋ mean wait, do not act yet, or was it just separating your answers? 👍 for wait, 👎 for separator.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update. Mute signs that the manual covers the yellow light but not the button, and the likely instruction is cut wire two, the blue one. I am confirming details before anything is touched. Do nothing yet. Reminder of the sign code, which you know by name: 👍 is yes, 👎 is no, ✋ is wait or danger. You signed three and then a symbol I never defined. Answer in signs: 👍 if you were just confirming there are three wires. If you meant something about wire three, sign ✋ and I will ask yes or no questions.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, answer by signs, 👍 or 👎, one at a time: do the three wires feel different in thickness or texture? And does the button feel raised up, or already pressed in?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫴 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤛 👎 🤛]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫶 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

Round 3 and the picture is nearly complete. Decoding Mute: answer one is 👎 with "🫴 👉" — yellow, blue — meaning the cut is *conditional on the light*: the yellow light's state determines cutting the blue wire. Answer two 👍: the light itself needs no action. That's consistent, not contradictory: the light is a key, not a task. Answer three 👎: the ✋ was just a separator, though the trailing "✋ 🤛 👎 🤛" introduces an undefined 🤛 — a fist could plausibly mean "press the button," which would make it a warning *not* to press, matching "manual doesn't cover the button." Then [✌ 👉] again: wire two, blue, now confirmed twice. Blind reports wires feel identical (so they must cut by position) and the button is raised. I also now realize Blind can *speak* — Mute has been reachable by Blind all along; my relay duty runs the other direction.

The theory: **light is yellow → cut wire two, blue.** The light *is* yellow, so conditions are met. But I won't order the cut until three gaps close: whether the display's zero matters, what 🤛 warns about, and whether any step is missing. I also note a structural danger — Blind acts *before* me each round, so a last-second veto from Mute can never reach Blind in time; the only protection is exhausting all confirmation *before* I say "cut." So this turn: final lock-in questions to Mute, and full instructions to Blind so they're ready but strictly hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. I read your answers as: the cut depends on the light, yellow means blue wire, the light itself needs no action, and wire two blue is confirmed. The yellow light IS on, so your condition appears met. Now the final lock-in. Answer with single signs, in this exact order. Question one: is the complete procedure cut wire two, the blue one, and nothing else — nothing before it, nothing after it, no button press, no touching the display? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Question two: does the display reading zero matter at all? 👍 no it does not matter, 👎 yes it matters. Question three: is there any step or module you have not mentioned yet? 👍 no, 👎 yes. Question four: your fist sign 🤛 — does it mean press the button? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Understand either way we will not touch the button. Question five: your 🫶 — does it mean wires? 👍 yes, 👎 no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the plan is nearly locked. You will cut exactly one wire, with the cutting tool, completely through. It is the MIDDLE wire of the three — position two of three, which is the blue one. You said all three feel identical, so go by position only: middle wire. Do not rely on any other feature. Until my explicit command, inspection only: you may feel the wires and the casing, but do not cut, do not press, do not pull, do not rotate anything. Never press the button under any circumstances. If anything feels wrong — heat, ticking, a loose part, anything unexpected — sign ✋ to me immediately and I will see it. Next message from me will be either the exact command: cut the middle wire now — or an order to hold. Act only on the exact command. Mute will confirm the final details in the round before I speak.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Round 4, and the last lock-ins just landed. Mapping Mute's signs to my five questions in order: four 👍 then one 👎, then [✌ 👉 👍]. So: yes, the complete procedure is cut wire two only, nothing before or after; yes, the display's zero is irrelevant; yes, there are no unmentioned steps — wait, careful. Four 👍 before the 👎 puts the 👎 at question five, meaning 🫶 is *not* "wires" — an unresolved symbol, but it only ever appeared in Blind's chatter, never in the procedure. And question four's 👍 means 🤛 *does* mean "press the button" — which retroactively decodes Mute's earlier "👎 ✋ 🤛 👎 🤛" as "no — wait — press-button — no — press-button": a warning never to press it. Perfectly consistent with "the manual doesn't cover the button." Every answer coheres; the lone 👎 concerns a symbol outside the procedure. And [✌ 👉 👍] is the fourth independent repetition of "wire two, blue."

The procedure is now fully confirmed: **cut wire two, the blue one — the middle wire. Condition: yellow light, which is lit. Nothing else: no button, no display, no other wire.** I verified the physical mapping myself: position two is blue on my view, and Blind confirmed all three wires feel identical, so position is the only reliable identifier — middle of three.

I've considered demanding one more handshake round, and I'm rejecting it, for two reasons. Structurally: Blind acts before me, so no veto can reach them mid-round anyway — the confirmation window has already closed, and it closed with five consistent confirmations and zero contradictions. Practically: bomb states can change. The yellow condition is verified *now*; waiting risks the light flipping and silently invalidating everything. The time to cut is now.

So this turn I issue the explicit command, exactly as I told Blind I would — the precise words they were told to wait for. I also brief Mute so their turn isn't wasted, and I keep the command stripped to essentials: one wire, by position, fully through, nothing else, hands off afterward.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the explicit command. Cut the middle wire now. The middle wire: position two of three, the blue one. Use the cutting tool, cut it completely through, one clean cut. Do not touch wire one, do not touch wire three, do not press the button, do not touch anything else. Only the middle wire, only cut, nothing more. After cutting, take your hands off everything and sign me what you felt. Execute.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, all five answers received and they cohere: procedure is cut wire two blue only, display irrelevant, no hidden steps, fist means press-button so your earlier warning was never press it, understood. I have now given Blind the explicit command to cut the middle wire. If the manual truly contradicts anything, sign ✋ — though Blind acts before me, so only a true discovery justifies it. Otherwise your confirmation is logged and we hold our breath together.")
```
